subject: AI & Agents
title: Transfer Learning: One Model, Many Skills
description: A 60-second lesson on Transfer Learning: One Model, Many Skills.

hook.text: A model trained to write English can suddenly translate French. Nobody taught it French specifically.

buildup.text: Transfer learning means skills learned in one domain carry over to related tasks.

discovery.text: A pre-trained LLM can be fine-tuned for medicine, law, or code with relatively little extra data.

twist.text: This is why foundation models are so valuable — one model serves as the base for thousands of apps.

climax.text: GPT-4 wasn't trained to write sonnets or debug Python specifically. It learned both from general text.

punchline.text: Learn language deeply, and everything else comes along for the ride.

quiz.question: What is transfer learning?
options: Skills from one task carry over to help with related tasks
Copying one model's weights into another
Teaching a model two languages at once

details.summary: Transfer learning lets a model trained on one task apply its knowledge to different tasks. Pre-trained language models transfer their general understanding to new domains through fine-tuning, saving enormous time and compute.
details.whyItMatters: Without transfer learning, every AI application would need training from scratch. It makes AI practical for specialized domains by building on existing general capabilities rather than starting over.
takeaways: Transfer learning reuses knowledge from one task for another
It saves the enormous cost of training from scratch
Fine-tuning adapts general models to specific domains efficiently

faq.question: How does transfer learning save resources?
faq.answer: Training a model from scratch costs millions of dollars and months of compute. Transfer learning starts with an already-trained model and adapts it with a fraction of the data and compute, often in hours.

faq.question: What kinds of knowledge transfer between tasks?
faq.answer: Grammar, reasoning patterns, world knowledge, and general language understanding all transfer well. Domain-specific jargon and specialized reasoning require additional fine-tuning on relevant data.
